sections.title: Form and coastal habitat
sections.text: Plantago maritima, sea plantain, is a low perennial of salt marshes and coastal bluffs. Its fleshy, narrow leaves, mostly 5–25 cm long, form a basal rosette; flowering stalks are about 5–25 cm tall.

sections.title: Flowers and food
sections.text: Dense flower spikes are about 2–10 cm long. NatureScot reports that the leaves are eaten raw or cooked and the seeds can also be eaten or ground into flour.

sections.title: Identification
sections.text: Its narrow, fleshy leaves suit coastal habitats and distinguish it from the broader-leaved P. major. Correct identification matters: sea arrowgrass, Triglochin maritima, is a similar-looking plant that should not be confused with it.
